entities.name: Trypanosomiasis
entities.description: A complex neglected tropical protozoan disease caused by kinetoplastid parasites of the genus Trypanosoma, encompassing American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, featuring acute chagoma/Romaña sign and chronic dilated cardiomyopathy with apical aneurysm/RBBB or digestive megasyndromes) and Human African Trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense or Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, featuring chancre, Winterbottom cervical adenopathy, and progressive sleep-wake cycle inversion with meningoencephalitis).

entities.name: Nocturnal Triatomine Kissing Bug Feces Contamination in Endemic Rural Latin America
entities.description: Vector-borne exposure to nocturnal hematophagous triatomine bugs (family Reduviidae, subfamily Triatominae; kissing bugs such as Triatoma infestans and Rhodnius prolixus) infesting cracked adobe walls and thatch roofs in rural Latin America, which feed on sleeping hosts and defecate metacyclic trypomastigotes that are rubbed into bite wounds or mucous membranes.

entities.name: Oral Ingestion of Fresh Juices Contaminated with Crushed Triatomine Vectors
entities.description: Foodborne exposure via ingestion of unpasteurized sugarcane juice, fresh açaí pulp, or meals contaminated with crushed infected triatomines or opossum secretions, triggering explosive point-source outbreaks of acute severe Chagas myocarditis with high mortality.

entities.name: Blood Product Transfusion, Organ Transplantation, or Congenital Maternal-Fetal Exposure
entities.description: Non-vector transmission pathways of Trypanosoma cruzi including transplacental congenital transmission from infected mothers, transfusion of unscreened blood/platelet products, and solid organ transplantation, responsible for emerging cases in both endemic countries and global non-endemic metropolitan centers.

entities.name: Daytime Tsetse Fly Bite in Sub-Saharan African Riverine or Savannah Habitats
entities.description: Vector-borne exposure via the painful daytime bite of infected tsetse flies (genus Glossina): riverine Glossina palpalis species transmitting T. b. gambiense in Western and Central Africa, or savannah Glossina morsitans species transmitting T. b. rhodesiense in Eastern and Southern Africa.

entities.name: Exposure to East African Game and Cattle Reservoirs in Rhodesiense Habitats
entities.description: Occupational or recreational exposure (safari travelers, park rangers, cattle pastoralists) in East and Southern African savannah woodlands where wild game ungulates and domestic cattle serve as primary zoonotic reservoirs for virulent Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense.

entities.name: Trypanosoma cruzi
entities.description: Kinetoplastid protozoan parasite and intracellular hemoflagellate that proliferates as intracellular amastigotes within cardiac myocytes, enteric smooth muscle, and autonomic ganglia, and circulates as extracellular motile C-shaped trypomastigotes in blood, causing Chagas disease.

entities.name: Trypanosoma brucei gambiense
entities.description: Extracellular hemoflagellate protozoan parasite responsible for anthroponotic, slowly progressive, chronic Human African Trypanosomiasis across 24 countries of West and Central Africa, accounting for over 90% of reported sleeping sickness cases.

entities.name: Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense
entities.description: Extracellular hemoflagellate protozoan parasite causing acute, virulent, rapidly fulminant zoonotic Human African Trypanosomiasis in Eastern and Southern Africa, causing rapid parasitemia, early neurovascular invasion, and myocarditis.

entities.name: Romaña Sign Unilateral Painless Periorbital Edema and Conjunctivitis
entities.description: Unilateral, painless, bipalpebral violaceous edema with ipsilateral conjunctivitis and non-tender preauricular lymphadenopathy resulting from T. cruzi contamination of the ocular mucous membranes, pathognomonic of acute Chagas disease present in up to 50% of acute ocular inoculations.

entities.name: Inoculation Chagoma Indurated Violaceous Skin Nodule
entities.description: Indurated, erythematous, violaceous inflammatory skin nodule appearing at the cutaneous portal of entry of Trypanosoma cruzi following triatomine bite and defecation, frequently accompanied by local satellite lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Chagasic Cardiomyopathy with Apical Aneurysm and Right Bundle Branch Block
entities.description: Severe chronic dilated cardiomyopathy characterized by biventricular systolic failure, localized left ventricular apical dyskinesia or thinning (pathognomonic apical aneurysm), mural thrombus formation predisposing to cardioembolic stroke, and conduction system disease presenting with Right Bundle Branch Block and Left Anterior Fascicular Block.

entities.name: Chagasic Megaesophagus with Progressive Dysphagia and Regurgitation
entities.description: Severe esophageal motricity disorder resulting from destruction of myenteric (Auerbach) parasympathetic plexus neurons, manifesting as progressive dysphagia for solids and liquids, odynophagia, regurgitation of undigested meals, nocturnal pulmonary aspiration, and profound cachexia.

entities.name: Chagasic Megacolon with Severe Obstipation and Fecaloma Impaction
entities.description: Severe colonic dilatation and hypomotility secondary to enteric parasympathetic neuronal loss, leading to intractable chronic obstipation (defecation once every 2–4 weeks), massive abdominal distension and meteorism, impaction of stony-hard fecalomas, and high risk of acute sigmoid volvulus.

entities.name: Winterbottom Sign Posterior Cervical Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Prominent, non-tender, rubbery, mobile lymph node enlargement localized to the posterior cervical triangle of the neck, serving as the classical admission physical hallmark of hemolymphatic Stage 1 T. b. gambiense sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Trypanosomal Chancre at Tsetse Bite Site
entities.description: Painful, tender, indurated, erythematous nodule developing at the site of an infected tsetse fly bite within days of inoculation, typically desquamating or ulcerating centrally, especially common in T. b. rhodesiense.

entities.name: Severe Sleep-Wake Cycle Inversion and Daytime Somnolence
entities.description: Circadian sleep rhythm fragmentation pathognomonic of Stage 2 meningoencephalitic African sleeping sickness, characterized by uncontrollable daytime somnolence and sleep attacks alternating with intractable nocturnal insomnia, motor agitation, and progressive neuropsychiatric decay.

entities.name: Direct Blood Microscopy of Motile C-Shaped Trypomastigotes
entities.description: Direct microscopic identification of motile, extracellular, flagellated C-shaped trypomastigotes on fresh anticoagulated blood wet mounts, microhematocrit centrifugation (Woo test), or Giemsa-stained thin/thick blood smears during acute Chagas disease or Stage 1 African trypanosomiasis.

entities.name: Dual Concordant Positive Serological Assays for Anti-T. cruzi IgG
entities.description: Mandatory laboratory confirmation for chronic Chagas disease requiring two separate, concordantly reactive serological assays (e.g., ELISA, indirect immunofluorescence, or indirect hemagglutination) using different parasite antigenic preparations, due to subpatent parasitemia.

entities.name: 12-Lead ECG Showing Right Bundle Branch Block and Left Anterior Fascicular Block
entities.description: Admission 12-lead electrocardiogram demonstrating bifascicular conduction delay with complete Right Bundle Branch Block (RBBB) and Left Anterior Fascicular Block (LAFB), frequent ventricular premature beats, or complete atrioventricular block in chronic Chagasic cardiomyopathy.

entities.name: Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Apical Thinning and Aneurysm with Thrombus
entities.description: Transthoracic echocardiogram revealing segmental wall-motion abnormalities, global systolic dysfunction, and localized left ventricular apical thinning or dyskinetic outpouching (apical aneurysm) frequently harboring mural thrombi.

entities.name: Barium Esophagogram Bird-Beak Distal Narrowing and Megacolon Dilatation
entities.description: Fluoroscopic barium contrast imaging demonstrating marked esophageal dilation with distal smooth tapering (bird-beak sign or pencil-tip narrowing) on esophagogram, and massive elongation and dilation of the sigmoid colon (dolichomegacolon) on barium enema.

entities.name: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis, Elevated Protein, and Mott Morular Cells
entities.description: Staging lumbar puncture findings in Stage 2 Human African Trypanosomiasis demonstrating CSF leukocyte count > 5 WBC/mcL, elevated total protein (> 45 mg/dL), centrifuged CSF trypomastigotes, and Mott morular plasma cells containing IgM inclusions.

entities.name: Positive Card Agglutination Test for Trypanosomiasis in Gambiense HAT
entities.description: Rapid serological agglutination assay (CATT) detecting circulating antibodies against variable surface glycoprotein antigens of T. b. gambiense in whole blood or serum, used for triage screening in West/Central African endemic areas.

entities.name: Absence of Travel, Residence, or Exposure in Endemic Latin American or Sub-Saharan Regions
entities.description: Complete absence of lifetime travel, residence, vector contact, or ancestral origin in rural Latin America (for Chagas) or sub-Saharan African tsetse fly belts (for HAT), without history of blood transfusion or organ transplant, virtually excluding trypanosomiasis.

entities.name: Normal 12-Lead Electrocardiogram and Normal Transthoracic Echocardiogram
entities.description: A strictly normal 12-lead ECG (no bundle branch block, fascicular block, or arrhythmias) and normal echocardiogram showing intact apical wall motion and normal chamber dimensions, virtually ruling out symptomatic Chagasic cardiomyopathy.

entities.name: Normal CSF Analysis with Cell Count Below 5 Cells per Microliter and Absent Trypanosomes
entities.description: Normal cerebrospinal fluid examination demonstrating leukocyte count < 5 cells/mcL, normal protein, and absence of trypanosomes or Mott cells, definitively ruling out Stage 2 meningoencephalitic African sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Negative Results on Two Concordant Distinct Anti-T. cruzi IgG Serologic Assays
entities.description: Non-reactive serologic results across two distinct, validated assays using different antigen preparations (e.g., negative ELISA and negative indirect immunofluorescence), ruling out chronic Chagas disease.

entities.name: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy and Ischemic Heart Disease
entities.description: Non-infectious cardiomyopathy and ischemic heart failure presenting with biventricular failure and cardiomegaly, differentiated from Chagas cardiomyopathy by diffuse global hypokinesia without apical thinning/aneurysm, absence of RBBB+LAFB bifascicular block, absence of digestive megasyndromes, and negative T. cruzi serology.

entities.name: Idiopathic Achalasia and Hirschsprung Disease
entities.description: Primary neuromuscular gastrointestinal motility disorders causing progressive dysphagia or severe obstipation, differentiated from Chagasic megadisease by the absence of concurrent cardiac apical aneurysms, absence of bundle branch conduction defects, negative T. cruzi serology, and lack of triatomine exposure.

entities.name: Severe Malaria
entities.description: Acute febrile infection caused by Plasmodium falciparum presenting with high cyclical fever, hemolytic anemia, and splenomegaly, differentiated from African trypanosomiasis by the presence of intraerythrocytic ring parasites on blood smears and absence of Winterbottom cervical adenopathy or sleep-wake cycle inversion.

entities.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Systemic kinetoplastid infection (Kala-azar) caused by Leishmania donovani/infantum presenting with prolonged undulating fever, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and hypergammaglobulinemia, differentiated by intracellular amastigotes inside macrophages on bone marrow aspirate and lack of extracellular flagellates, Winterbottom adenopathy, or apical aneurysms.

entities.name: Benznidazole Oral Therapy
entities.description: First-line oral nitroimidazole trypanocidal regimen (5–7 mg/kg/day for 60 days) providing high parasitological cure rates (>80%) in acute, congenital, and early chronic Chagas disease, but accompanied by frequent adverse effects (exfoliative dermatitis, peripheral neuropathy).

entities.name: Nifurtimox Oral Therapy
entities.description: Oral nitrofuran antiprotozoal therapy (8–10 mg/kg/day for 60–90 days) effective in acute Chagas disease, and also utilized as an oral component of combination therapy (NECT) for Stage 2 African sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Pentamidine Isethionate Intramuscular Regimen
entities.description: Intramuscular diamidine therapy (4 mg/kg/day for 7–10 days) achieving high cure rates in Stage 1 hemolymphatic Trypanosoma brucei gambiense sleeping sickness, but incapable of penetrating the blood-brain barrier for Stage 2 disease.

entities.name: Nifurtimox-Eflornithine Combination Therapy and Oral Fexinidazole
entities.description: Standard-of-care treatments for Stage 2 meningoencephalitic T. b. gambiense sleeping sickness: NECT (oral nifurtimox for 10 days plus IV eflornithine infusions for 7 days) and oral fexinidazole (with food for Stage 1 and non-severe Stage 2), achieving >95% cure with low neurotoxicity.

entities.name: Suramin Intravenous Regimen for Rhodesiense First Stage
entities.description: Intravenous polysulfonated naphthylamine therapy (20 mg/kg weekly up to 1 g for 5 doses) used specifically for first-stage hemolymphatic Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense infection, requiring renal monitoring.

entities.name: Melarsoprol Intravenous Organoarsenical Regimen
entities.description: Intravenous organoarsenical capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier for Stage 2 meningoencephalitic Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, effective but associated with a 5–10% risk of fatal post-treatment reactive encephalopathy.

entities.name: Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial and Antiviral Agents
entities.description: Inherent lack of clinical, microbiological, or parasitological response to broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal, or antiviral agents, confirming the necessity of targeted kinetoplastid antiprotozoal therapy.

entities.name: Refractoriness of Advanced Fibrotic Chagas Cardiomyopathy and Megasyndromes to Benznidazole
entities.description: Inability of antiparasitic therapy with benznidazole to reverse established transmural myocardial apical fibrosis, ventricular dilatation, or irreversible enteric neurolysis in advanced chronic Chagas disease, requiring supportive cardiac/surgical care.

relationships.target: Nocturnal Triatomine Kissing Bug Feces Contamination in Endemic Rural Latin America
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] American trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) is primarily transmitted through contamination of bite wounds or mucous membranes with metacyclic trypomastigote-containing feces of nocturnal triatomine bugs inhabiting rural dwellings in Latin America.

relationships.target: Oral Ingestion of Fresh Juices Contaminated with Crushed Triatomine Vectors
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Trypanosomiasis can be transmitted orally via ingestion of fresh juices (açai, sugarcane) contaminated with crushed infected triatomines, producing an explosive, severe acute Chagas myocarditis outbreak.

relationships.target: Blood Product Transfusion, Organ Transplantation, or Congenital Maternal-Fetal Exposure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis is acquired non-vectorially through transplacental vertical transmission, transfusions of contaminated blood products, or solid organ transplants from infected donors in both endemic and non-endemic regions.

relationships.target: Daytime Tsetse Fly Bite in Sub-Saharan African Riverine or Savannah Habitats
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Human African trypanosomiasis is transmitted by the painful daytime bite of infected Glossina tsetse flies in riverine or savannah ecozones of sub-Saharan Africa.

relationships.target: Exposure to East African Game and Cattle Reservoirs in Rhodesiense Habitats
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Human African trypanosomiasis caused by T. b. rhodesiense is linked to exposure to savannah wildlife and domestic cattle reservoirs in Eastern and Southern Africa.

relationships.target: Trypanosoma cruzi
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) is caused by the intracellular kinetoplastid protozoan Trypanosoma cruzi, which replicates inside cardiomyocytes and autonomic enteric plexuses.

relationships.target: Trypanosoma brucei gambiense
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Human African trypanosomiasis in West and Central Africa is caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense, producing a chronic, slowly progressive meningoencephalitic illness.

relationships.target: Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Human African trypanosomiasis in East and Southern Africa is caused by Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, producing an acute, virulent infection with rapid multi-organ and central nervous system invasion.

relationships.target: Romaña Sign Unilateral Painless Periorbital Edema and Conjunctivitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Romaña sign presents as unilateral, painless, bipalpebral periorbital edema and violaceous conjunctivitis with preauricular lymphadenopathy, representing the pathognomonic physical hallmark of acute ocular Chagas disease.

relationships.target: Inoculation Chagoma Indurated Violaceous Skin Nodule
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Inoculation chagoma manifests as an inflammatory, indurated, violaceous skin nodule at the site of triatomine bug defecation during the acute phase of Chagas disease.

relationships.target: Chagasic Cardiomyopathy with Apical Aneurysm and Right Bundle Branch Block
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Chronic Chagasic cardiomyopathy presents with biventricular heart failure, a pathognomonic left ventricular apical aneurysm, mural thrombosis predisposing to stroke, and bifascicular conduction defects (RBBB plus LAFB).

relationships.target: Chagasic Megaesophagus with Progressive Dysphagia and Regurgitation
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Chagasic megaesophagus presents at admission with progressive solid and liquid dysphagia, painful odynophagia, regurgitation of undigested meals, and severe cachexia secondary to enteric nervous system destruction.

relationships.target: Chagasic Megacolon with Severe Obstipation and Fecaloma Impaction
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Chagasic megacolon manifests with severe intractable obstipation, massive abdominal distension, impaction of stony-hard fecalomas, and acute sigmoid volvulus requiring surgical intervention.

relationships.target: Winterbottom Sign Posterior Cervical Lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Winterbottom sign presents as visible, painless, rubbery, mobile posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, serving as the classical admission physical hallmark of Stage 1 T. b. gambiense sleeping sickness.

relationships.target: Trypanosomal Chancre at Tsetse Bite Site
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] A trypanosomal chancre manifests as a painful, indurated, erythematous nodule at the site of a tsetse fly bite, appearing days before systemic dissemination, especially in T. b. rhodesiense.

relationships.target: Severe Sleep-Wake Cycle Inversion and Daytime Somnolence
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Circadian sleep disruption presents with pathognomonic sleep-wake cycle inversion, featuring uncontrollable daytime somnolence and nocturnal insomnia in Stage 2 meningoencephalitic sleeping sickness.

relationships.target: Direct Blood Microscopy of Motile C-Shaped Trypomastigotes
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission wet mounts, microhematocrit centrifugation (Woo test), or Giemsa smears confirm acute trypanosomiasis by visualizing motile extracellular flagellated C-shaped trypomastigotes in circulating blood.

relationships.target: Dual Concordant Positive Serological Assays for Anti-T. cruzi IgG
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Chronic Chagas disease diagnosis on admission requires two concordantly positive serological assays (such as ELISA and indirect immunofluorescence) using different T. cruzi antigenic preparations.

relationships.target: 12-Lead ECG Showing Right Bundle Branch Block and Left Anterior Fascicular Block
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission 12-lead ECG reveals a characteristic bifascicular conduction pattern of Right Bundle Branch Block (RBBB) combined with Left Anterior Fascicular Block (LAFB) in over 50% of chronic Chagasic cardiomyopathy patients.

relationships.target: Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Apical Thinning and Aneurysm with Thrombus
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission echocardiography reveals localized left ventricular apical thinning, dyskinetic apical aneurysm, and mural thrombi indicative of advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy.

relationships.target: Barium Esophagogram Bird-Beak Distal Narrowing and Megacolon Dilatation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Barium radiography demonstrates distal esophageal tapering with proximal dilation (bird-beak sign) and massive elongation/dilation of the sigmoid colon (dolichomegacolon) in Chagasic digestive megasyndromes.

relationships.target: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis, Elevated Protein, and Mott Morular Cells
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Staging lumbar puncture reveals CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (> 5 WBC/mcL), elevated protein (> 45 mg/dL), motile trypanosomes, and Mott morular plasma cells containing IgM inclusions, diagnosing Stage 2 African sleeping sickness.

relationships.target: Positive Card Agglutination Test for Trypanosomiasis in Gambiense HAT
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] High-titer positivity on the Card Agglutination Test for Trypanosomiasis (CATT) provides rapid admission serological screening confirmation for T. b. gambiense infection.

relationships.target: Absence of Travel, Residence, or Exposure in Endemic Latin American or Sub-Saharan Regions
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis is virtually ruled out in patients with zero epidemiological exposure or residency in endemic rural Latin America or sub-Saharan Africa, in the absence of blood/organ donation or congenital exposure.

relationships.target: Normal 12-Lead Electrocardiogram and Normal Transthoracic Echocardiogram
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Symptomatic Chagasic cardiomyopathy is effectively ruled out by a completely normal 12-lead ECG and normal echocardiogram showing preserved apical wall motion without conduction defects.

relationships.target: Normal CSF Analysis with Cell Count Below 5 Cells per Microliter and Absent Trypanosomes
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Second-stage meningoencephalitic African trypanosomiasis is ruled out by normal CSF cell count (< 5 WBC/mcL), absence of Mott cells, and absence of centrifuged CSF trypanosomes.

relationships.target: Negative Results on Two Concordant Distinct Anti-T. cruzi IgG Serologic Assays
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Chronic Chagas disease is ruled out by non-reactive results on two independent, validated serological assays detecting anti-T. cruzi antibodies.

relationships.target: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy and Ischemic Heart Disease
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis (Chagas cardiomyopathy) is differentiated from idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy and ischemic heart disease by the presence of pathognomonic apical LV aneurysm, RBBB with LAFB, positive T. cruzi serology, and associated digestive megasyndromes, whereas idiopathic DCM causes diffuse global hypokinesia without apical thinning.

relationships.target: Idiopathic Achalasia and Hirschsprung Disease
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from idiopathic achalasia and Hirschsprung disease by the presence of positive anti-T. cruzi serology, concurrent cardiac conduction abnormalities, apical aneurysms, and triatomine exposure in Latin America.

relationships.target: Severe Malaria
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from severe malaria because malaria exhibits intraerythrocytic parasites on blood smears and lacks Winterbottom posterior cervical adenopathy and characteristic sleep-wake cycle inversion.

relationships.target: Visceral Leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis because visceral leishmaniasis exhibits profound pancytopenia and intracellular amastigotes in bone marrow macrophages, whereas trypanosomiasis presents with extracellular flagellates, Winterbottom sign, or Chagasic apical aneurysm.

relationships.target: Benznidazole Oral Therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trypanosomiasis (acute, congenital, and early chronic Chagas disease) responds with high parasitological cure rates to oral benznidazole therapy, halting disease progression.

relationships.target: Nifurtimox Oral Therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trypanosomiasis responds to oral nifurtimox therapy in acute Chagas disease and as an essential oral component of combination therapy for Stage 2 gambiense sleeping sickness.

relationships.target: Pentamidine Isethionate Intramuscular Regimen
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trypanosomiasis in Stage 1 hemolymphatic T. b. gambiense sleeping sickness responds to intramuscular pentamidine isethionate, clearing peripheral parasitemia.

relationships.target: Nifurtimox-Eflornithine Combination Therapy and Oral Fexinidazole
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trypanosomiasis with Stage 2 CNS T. b. gambiense infection responds to Nifurtimox-Eflornithine Combination Therapy (NECT) and oral fexinidazole, achieving high cure rates with low neurotoxicity.

relationships.target: Suramin Intravenous Regimen for Rhodesiense First Stage
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trypanosomiasis caused by first-stage hemolymphatic T. b. rhodesiense responds to intravenous suramin therapy.

relationships.target: Melarsoprol Intravenous Organoarsenical Regimen
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trypanosomiasis in Stage 2 meningoencephalitic T. b. rhodesiense responds to intravenous melarsoprol, although therapy carries significant risk of reactive encephalopathy.

relationships.target: Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial and Antiviral Agents
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Trypanosomiasis is intrinsically resistant to standard broad-spectrum antibacterial and antiviral agents, showing no clinical improvement upon their administration.

relationships.target: Refractoriness of Advanced Fibrotic Chagas Cardiomyopathy and Megasyndromes to Benznidazole
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Established fibrotic lesions in advanced chronic Chagasic cardiomyopathy and end-stage digestive megacolon are refractory to parasitological reversal by benznidazole or nifurtimox, requiring supportive cardiac/surgical care.
